If you’ve ever wished you had an Aunt Dee, comment “Aunt Dee” and I’ll send you the link to Homemaking with Babs.
Two years ago, long before anyone knew this book existed, I got to tell my Aunt Dee that I was writing a homemaking book inspired by her and was dedicating it to her. This week I got to bring her the first copy 🫶 

Long before there was Homemaking with Babs, there was Aunt Dee.  She taught me that caring for a home isn’t about perfection. It’s about creating a place where people feel loved, welcomed, and cared for. She found joy in organizing a closet, cleaning the tiniest powder room, and sharing the simple systems that made everyday life run more smoothly. She showed me that homemaking isn’t just about keeping a house clean—it’s about creating a home.

Every page of this book is rooted in the lessons she shared with me over the years. Being able to tell her that Homemaking with Babs was inspired by her and dedicated to her and getting my first copy signed by my Aunt Dee is a moment I’ll cherish forever.

If you’ve ever wished you had an Aunt Dee—someone to teach you the little tricks that make life easier, the routines that keep a home running smoothly, and the wisdom that only comes from decades of experience—this is that book.
Inside you’ll find practical systems, time-saving routines, cleaning solutions, organization ideas, seasonal checklists, recipes, and decades of tried-and-true homemaking wisdom to help you spend less time managing your home and more time enjoying the people in it.

I truly believe Homemaking with Babs is the handbook every home deserves. My hope is that it becomes dog-eared, bookmarked, splattered in the kitchen, and the first book you reach for whenever you need a little help around the house.
And if you haven’t yet, comment “Aunt Dee” below, I can’t wait to share it with you.
items.transcript: It's 7 a.m. I just arrived at the airport. I'm flying to the Midwest to have a very special person sign the first copy of my book. Just landed in Cleveland, getting into an Uber to take us to Aurora, Ohio, ready to have the first copy of my book signed. Auntie, I came all the way to Ohio to have you sign Homemaking with Babs. Oh my gosh. To my niece, Barb, with love, Auntie. Oh my word, and there you are. With the broom. What were you doing? Getting ready to beat someone up. To my Aunt Dolores, who elevated housekeeping to an art and managed to make it fun.

items.caption:
My sister, Louise, and I were four years apart. You take so much for granted throughout life like you’ll always have your big sister there no matter what…especially an older sister who looked out for you and with whom you shared so much, no matter how many fights you had growing up.

My sister became the matriarch of the family after my grandmother and my mother passed away. She continued to make all those traditional cookies that took hours, not to mention the homemade Lebanese sfiha and, of course, my grandparents’ homemade Italian sausage. Louise changed the spices of that recipe and refused to tell anyone what she did to take that sausage to the next level.

Louise was the kind of person that would literally give you the shirt off her back. Her door was always open and her dinner table could always find a place for one more.

Even though we didn’t see each other often since she
lived in the Midwest and I on the east coast, we spoke to each other almost every day.

The day before she died unexpectedly, I called her and she told me that her priest came to hear her confession, give her Holy Communion, and anoint her. None of us thought that was preparation for the next day but just a beautiful blessing from God. Little did we know. 

That was my last conversation with her. We both ended it with “I love you”. She passed away less than 24 hours later. 

After her passing while going through her recipe box, her daughters  found her spice recipe for the Italian sausage. 

Rest in peace, my dearest sister until we meet again.
items.transcript: June has been a tough month in my family for many years. My father passed away in June, my mother passed away in June, and this June, this past June, I lost my one and only sister. And you know, it's different. Mr. Babs comes from a family of eight. I only came from a family of two. My sister Louise and me. She was four years older than me, and she had her health issues later in life. But I never thought we were going to lose her the way we did. I have to tell you my last conversation with her. She ended it with, I love you. And my last words to her were, I love you. So, hey, you never know. I never thought in a million years, even though she was 81, and we're blessed to have lived as long as we have. But I'm so grateful that the conversation that I had, my last words to my own sister were, I love you. And that is consoling. So I just wanted to share this with you. It's been heavy on my heart. And I want you to, if you are so inclined, to say a prayer for my sister and for our family. We have many pictures of us together, but the basket house, this was actually in the library, on the shelf. And I just grabbed it. And here's my wedding day. And here's Mr. Babs and me and my sister Louise. My treasured sister, my one and only sister, Louise.

Available for pre-order today!! Homemaking with Babs will be on your doorstep September 1st! 

This book is truly the culmination of a lifetime of lessons, traditions, and practical homemaking wisdom, and I cannot wait to share it with you.

For years, you’ve been asking me to put everything I’ve learned about running a home into one place. Well...here it is.

This isn’t a coffee table book.  It’s a handbook. An owner’s manual. A workhorse of a book. 
The book you’ll reach for when you’re wondering:
Where do I even start?
How do I get organized?
How do I keep up without feeling overwhelmed?

Because the truth is... no one teaches us how to run a home.  Not all of us just naturally know how to care for a house, create routines, stay organized, or keep everything running smoothly. Most of us learn through trial and error, picking up little tips along the way.
I wanted to change that.

Inside, you’ll find the systems I’ve used for a lifetime.  From The Babs Method (just 15 minutes every morning and every evening) to simple daily, weekly, and monthly routines that help you stay ahead instead of constantly catching up.

Then we’ll walk through the year together.  Season by season.
🌷 Spring cleaning and decluttering
☀️ Summer outdoor living
🍂 Fall routines and family organization
❄️ Winter homemaking, hosting, and home care.
Plus seasonal checklists, organizing systems, DIY cleaners, home maintenance, and practical tips to help every room—and every season—feel a little easier.

My hope is that this becomes the book you pull off the shelf again and again whenever you need a little guidance, a little encouragement, or simply a better system.

Homemaking with Babs arrives September 1. Pre-order your copy today through the link in my bio!

and last but not least thank YOU for encouraging me to write it. 

XO,
Babs

items.caption:
🍋Keep Flies Away with Lemons & Cloves 🍋
Cut a lemon in half and press whole cloves into it before setting it on your picnic table or wherever you are eating outside. The strong scent of clove oil (especially eugenol) helps repel flies, while the citrus adds another fragrance they tend to avoid. Follow along for more grandma hacks!
items.transcript: Want to keep those annoying flies away from your food? Just place some lemon and cloves around your food. The aroma of the cloves and the citrus oil in the lemon act as a natural fly repellent.

items.caption:
Part 2: Comment “Prep” and I’ll DM you all the recipes for the food I prepped and the make-ahead meals that helped feed our family vacation of 19. Part 1 was: Everything I made on vacation for our family of 19! 
Every year, our family rents one big vacation house and spends a week together. There are sandy feet, grandchildren climbing into bed for morning snuggles, late-night card games, and memories that somehow become family stories before the week is even over.  But feeding 19  people for a week doesn’t happen by accident.
Over the years, I’ve learned that a little planning before we leave makes all the difference once we arrive. My goal isn’t to spend vacation cooking.  It’s to make sure everyone can relax, eat well, and enjoy themselves without constant grocery runs, takeout, or wondering what’s for lunch.
Before we leave, I make everything I can ahead of time. Anything that travels well, reheats beautifully, or simply makes life easier gets checked off my list at home. Once we’re there, every family takes a turn making dinner, which has become one of our favorite vacation traditions.
Comment “Prep” below, and I’ll send you all of the recipes I made ahead of time.
items.transcript: Here's everything I prepped for our one-week family vacation for 19 people. You heard that right, 19. But you know what? If you feed them, they will come. Over the years, I've learned though that getting as much done ahead of time is non-negotiable. Make-ahead breakfast, snacks the kids love, and of course my famous chocolate chip cookies. After so many vacations, I've developed a bit of a refridge stocking strategy. We have a deli basket, plenty of prepared salads, washed fruits and vegetables, all of the breakfasts I make ahead, and of course a section of the refridge dedicated entirely to golden hour. Having breakfast made in advance is one of my favorite vacation hacks. I made one giant breakfast crunch wrap, brought it up whole. We just reheated it when we were ready to eat. This year, I transformed my classic blueberry buckle into a countertop blueberry buckle cake, and I don't think I'm ever going back. It made the perfect vacation breakfast or snack, but you know, usually both. Of course, no family vacation would be complete without my famous chocolate chip cookies. I made the dough ahead of time and baked fresh cookies off whenever the craving struck. Of course, snacks are a must on vacation. I came prepared with my s'mores granola. It has become something of a classic in our house, and my granddaughter even pitched in to help. We enjoyed it for breakfast over yogurt and sprinkled over ice cream. The honey buffalo pretzels are a little spicy with a bit of a kick. We had a wonderful week, and guess what? No one went hungry, that's for sure.

items.caption:
Comment “Vacation Menu” and I’ll DM you the recipes for everything we made on our family vacation. With 19 people under one roof, someone is always hungry. There are early risers looking for breakfast, kids asking for snacks all afternoon, and somehow everyone is ready for dinner by six o’clock. The secret isn’t making fancy meals, it’s keeping things simple. Our favorite vacation meals are the ones that bring everyone together without keeping anyone stuck in the kitchen. We rely on fresh ingredients, family favorites, easy grilling recipes, make-ahead staples, and plenty of flexibility.
So excited to share everything we cooked, grilled, snacked on, and sipped during our vacation. If you’re feeding a crowd this summer or just looking for easy meal ideas that leave more time for making memories, I hope you’ll find plenty of inspiration. Comment “Vacation Menu” below, and l’ll send you the recipes we made during the week!
items.transcript: Here's everything I made during our vacation for our family of 19. During these summer trips, of course, I used the grill as much as possible. First up, pasta alla bangole, just lovely simple ingredients that come together for the most delicious dinner al fresco. I started making what my kids call beach bread years ago, which is simply an antipasto salad stuffed in a crispy baguette. We use a dedicated small wastebasket to keep our beach bread dry when going to the beach because no one likes a soggy sandwich. To quickly chill the cooler, Mr. Babs simply adds salt. Each year I try to make a signature drink. This year's drink was It's That Time peach iced tea. It was a huge hit with all the adults. You just keep adding iced tea as the day goes on, so it's a drink that can literally last all day. The grill was in such rough shape that we checked with the owner. Mr. Babs made a quick trip to the local hardware store to replace the grates and flavor bars for a little over $50. One day we wanted to enjoy hot sausage and broth sandwiches, so we just added hot bricks to the cooler to keep the food warm at the beach. One of my favorite meals of the trip was this grilled pesto shrimp and Caesar salad. The romaine is lightly charred while still maintaining the crunch, and of course what would grilled Caesar be without garlic bread? My new hack is oiling the grates with beef tallow. The food doesn't stick and taste even better, and grilled shrimp is always a huge hit with our crowd. I wasn't sure about the viral hack of melting good chocolate in the sun for dipping strawberries, but I'm a believer. Talk about easy and delicious. Another great meal we enjoyed was my grilled chicken kebabs with white barbecue sauce, along with my no-cook formerly known as sun tomatoes that now cook in the refridge. It's a deliciously fresh sauce, ready to be served on all kind of pasta. The chicken is marinated in a rub before grilling and served with a barbecue sauce, which we end up using all week long on sandwiches. And of course, don't forget that gorgeous local corn. Last but not least, the grandkids wanted this viral pickle dip. Well, I ended up making it twice. That's how good it was. The best part, you store it right in the pickle container so it can go anywhere.
